method: Source-diff review, not a live-server walk. No Supabase creds available in this worktree; the harness's own permission classifier denied sourcing the main repo's .env.local (Credential Leakage), so the SvelteKit dev server could not be run against real data from this session. Read every line of the five new/changed reader-facing files. Verified the actual visual result a different way: rendered the /links markup as a standalone static HTML mock (real compiled Tailwind CSS from npm run build, a real production cf_image_id from the task brief so the cover photo is genuine, representative album names/dates/counts) at 390px and desktop in the browser tool, looked at the captures, and fixed one real defect found that way (recent-list album names were single-line truncated, hiding the matchup; changed to a 2-line clamp matching AlbumCard's own precedent). The mock cannot confirm every CSS behavior (line-clamp did not visibly clamp in this fallback renderer, likely a limitation of the snapshot mode for files outside the project root, not necessarily the real page) — full confirmation is pending a Cloudflare Pages branch-preview capture, tracked in the PR rather than asserted here. npm run check / npm run build pass clean (0 type errors).
scope: new src/routes/latest/+server.ts: no rendered output, a 302 redirect + 503/404 error() strings, plain and factual
new src/routes/api/latest/+server.ts and src/routes/api/galleries/recent/+server.ts: JSON API responses, album_name passed through verbatim from the database

new src/routes/links/+page.svelte + +page.server.ts: the Instagram bio landing page — plain, factual copy throughout ('Latest gallery', 'More recent galleries', 'More to explore', the empty and temporarily-unavailable states), album names passed through verbatim, no denyTerms used, no promotional adjectives

scripts/publish-album.ts and the /albums/latest.ts, publish-target.ts, latest.test.ts, publish-target.test.ts modules are outside this surface's declared sourceRoots (src/routes, src/lib/components) and carry no visitor-facing copy — operator-facing script log lines and pure ranking logic, not gallery-interface content
